:::{#cor-mvn-uncorrelated-indpt}
#### For a multivariate normal vector, uncorrelated components are independent

If $\vX \sim \Normal_p\paren{\vecf{\mean}, \matr{\covmat}}$,
then $X_1, \ldots, X_p$ are independent
if and only if $\matr{\covmat}$ is diagonal,
that is, if and only if $\Covs{X_i}{X_j} = 0$ for every $i \neq j$.

:::

::: proof

By @thm-mvn-moments, $\Varf{\vX} = \matr{\covmat}$,
whose $(i,j)$-th element is $\Covs{X_i}{X_j}$
([elements of the variance matrix](variance-covariance.qmd#thm-vcov-elements)).
If $\matr{\covmat}$ is diagonal,
the components are independent by @thm-mvn-diagonal-indpt.
If the components are independent, then:

- each pair $X_i, X_j$ with $i \neq j$ is independent,
- each $X_i$ is continuous, with the density left
  after integrating out the other coordinates of the joint density
  ([marginal density from a joint density](random-variables.qmd#thm-marginal-density),
  with $p$ variables), and
- $\E{X_i^2} < \infty$,
  because $\Var{X_i}$, the $(i,i)$-th element of $\matr{\covmat}$, is defined,
  and a [variance](variance-covariance.qmd#def-variance) is defined
  only when $\E{X_i^2} < \infty$.

So $\matr{\covmat}$ is diagonal by
[independent components give a diagonal variance matrix](variance-covariance.qmd#cor-vcov-indpt-diagonal).

:::
